name: Palmitoylethanolamide
description: Palmitoylethanolamide (CAS 544-31-0 ), commonly abbreviated as PEA, is a fatty acid amide produced from palmitic acid and ethanolamine. Known in industrial contexts as palmitic acid monoethanolamide, it functions as a surface-active agent and emulsifier. This versatile compound is utilized across pharmaceutical and personal care manufacturing. In pharmaceutical formulations, PEA is incorporated as an active ingredient in oral and topical dosage forms where high purity is required. Regulatory-grade purity and consistent particle size are critical sourcing criteria for manufacturers. Personal care producers use it as an emulsifier and foam stabilizer in cleansing systems, shampoos, and skin creams. The material contributes significantly to texture and product stability in various applications. In cosmetic formulations, it supports emulsification of oil-water systems, reducing the need for additional co-emulsifiers. Industrial surface treatment processes use palmitic acid monoethanolamide as a wetting and dispersing agent. These properties help to improve substrate adhesion and coating uniformity in specialized manufacturing environments. The product is supplied as a white to off-white powder or waxy solid. Pharmaceutical and nutraceutical applications are served by micronized and ultramicronized grades to meet specific formulation needs. These grades differ in particle size distribution and bioavailability profile, which is a key specification decision for formulators. Technical and cosmetic grades are also available for non-pharmaceutical applications. Our supply chain ensures that all batches meet rigorous quality standards such as USP and EP .
